channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] France: Hundreds arrested as student protests escalate
item.description: Student protests have grown in scale and intensity, with violent clashes in some places leading to hundreds of arrests and dozens of injuries.

item.title: [Financial Times] Top Man City sponsor threatens legal action against Premier League
item.description: Etihad Airways says football body’s communication on critical report into club has ‘damaging implications’

item.title: [DW] Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
item.description: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers for rejected asylum seekers outside the EU.

item.title: [EU Observer] The EU’s ‘return regulation’ makes your home fair game for police — and Belgium is racing to use it
item.description: The EU's return regulation is being formally adopted on Thursday, setting a new precedent for police raids. The Belgians are pressing ahead with their own national version, putting civil liberties of everyone at risk.

item.title: [EU Observer] Where Russian maps place the occupiers, and where they really are — an overview of parts of the front (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,679)
item.description: Ukraine is losing the battle in the skies but holding strong on the battleground. And Russian media highlight “liberated” villages, but in reality they are still under Ukrainian control.

item.title: [EU Observer] US civil society groups call on EU not to delay methane rules
item.description: As Brussels moves to delay its methane rules, nearly 100 US civil society groups are urging EU governments not to cave to oil and gas lobbyists and the White House.

item.title: [EU Observer] Let’s not allow AI firms to use fears of future dystopias to distract Europeans from existing problems
item.description: As Big Tech companies dramatise rogue AI and China fears, the real fight is over who pays the price for today’s fraud, failures and job threats — and who pockets the productivity gains.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia elections: Polls overshadowed by exhaustion, exodus and geopolitics as ethnic politics eclipse real problems
item.description: Bosnia goes to the polls on October 4 to elect several parliaments and presidents. While voters worry about the economy and emigration, the campaign is focused on ethnicity, exposing the country's political paralysis.

item.title: [EU Observer] Israeli outpost-linked firms exploit loophole to buy up European property even as the EU curbs trade with illegal settlements
item.description: From a €4m holiday resort in rural Finland to demolished Bedouin villages in the Negev, the same Israeli developer exposes how Europe’s new trade curbs on settlements still leave the door wide open for settlement-linked firms to profit on EU soil.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Ceuta crisis shows how EU border outsourcing puts children at risk, says German lawyer
item.description: By outsourcing border control to Morocco, Turkey or Albania and then panicking when they “open the gates,” German lawyer Lena Riemer says EU capitals have handed hostile regimes a cheap, reliable way to divide and humiliate Europe.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] 70% of Montenegro supports EU membership – so will it happen in 2028? We ask lead MEP Marjan Šarec
item.description: EUobserver spoke to Marjan Šarec, former Slovenian prime minister, MEP for Renew Europe, and the parliament’s rapporteur for Montenegro. He's keeping his optimism for the country’s accession.

item.title: [DW] Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding.
item.description: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Did the Spanish government address the protesters’ demands on housing?
item.description: The Spanish government strengthens tenants' rights amidst pressure from hundreds of protesters in Madrid.

item.title: [EU Observer] Divided EU cyber defence faces real-life Russian and Chinese threats
item.description: From phishing attacks on Polish soldiers to near-blackouts in winter, the EU’s fragmented cyber defence is seeing Russian online threats spill into real‑world dangers for ordinary Europeans.

item.title: [DW] Hungary's reckoning with Orban's corrupt system picks up speed
item.description: Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar vowed to dismantle Orban's corrupt networks. High-profile figures are being arrested and many Hungarians are pushing for swift accountability, but the rule of law takes time.

item.title: [DW] UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
item.description: Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.

item.title: [DW] Albania: As corruption cases multiply, experts question whether the anti-corruption drive is addressing the causes or just the symptoms.
item.description: From a former president to the ex-intelligence chief, Albania is prosecuting senior officials at a rate once thought impossible. But do more prosecutions mean less corruption or simply better enforcement?

item.title: [DW] UK: US government questions bail for Fairford base suspects
item.description: The US government sees "the hand of a foreign actor" in the security scare at RAF Fairford, a hub for US heavy bombers in Europe. Donald Trump criticized the suspects being released on bail amid ongoing investigations.

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘We have not delivered’: Germany’s Wadephul criticizes slow EU enlargement progress
item.description: Germany's foreign minister warns that Europe risks losing credibility in the Western Balkans.

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘Thank you, Andy’: Farage gloats as Burnham reopens Brexit fight
item.description: The Reform UK leader used a speech in a Brexit-supporting Labour heartland to claim reopening the EU debate presents the "biggest boost" to his career.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Diesel américain : la France et quatre autres pays européens s’accordent sur une réponse “ferme”
item.description: Ces pays et la Commission européenne ont tenu jeudi une réunion d’urgence pour répondre aux appels lancés par les Etats-Unis en faveur d’un déblocage des réserves de carburant.

item.title: [Financial Times] Global bond sell-off pushes 10-year Treasury yield to highest since 2002
item.description: Sovereign debt costs around world return to multiyear highs

item.title: [Politico Europe] Lecornu à quitte ou double
item.description: Après avoir dévoilé jeudi son budget pour 2027, Sébastien Lecornu va engager une longue bataille politique pour tenter de le faire adopter avant la fin de l’année. Ordonnances ou 49.3 : quels sont les scénarios sur la table ? Comment le projet de loi de finances a-t-il été construit pour amadouer les oppositions ? Quelles […]

item.title: [Financial Times] EU countries in crisis talks over release of diesel stocks
item.description: Trump administration has pressured European countries to release strategic reserves, warning that it could ban US diesel exports if they do not do so

item.title: [Politico Europe] Europäische Länder vereinbaren „entschlossene“ Reaktion auf Diesel-Druck aus den USA
item.description: Die Länder, darunter Großbritannien, Frankreich und Deutschland, hielten am Donnerstag eine Krisensitzung ab, um auf die Forderungen der Trump-Regierung nach einer Freigabe ihrer Dieselreserven zu reagieren.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Comment les patrons de Meta et Nvidia ont œuvré en coulisses pour l’accord de la Maison-Blanche sur l’IA
item.description: Mark Zuckerberg et Jensen Huang ont cherché à mobiliser des soutiens en faveur des accords “moralement contraignants”, signés par Donald Trump et des dirigeants de la tech.

item.title: [Politico Europe] It’s war, not hybrid attacks, says Estonian foreign minister
item.description: Margus Tsahkna says Europe must present a united front against Moscow.

item.title: [Politico Europe] European countries agree on ‘assertive’ response to US pressure on diesel
item.description: The countries, including Britain, France and Germany, held an emergency meeting Thursday to respond to calls from the Trump administration to release fuel reserves.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Macron’s final budget hinges on Le Pen’s backing … for now
item.description: Paris is proposing €43B in savings to get the budget deficit down to 5% of GDP.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Wie Trumps Energieminister die EU zur Freigabe von Dieselreserven drängt
item.description: Mehrere EU-Staaten – darunter Deutschland – wurden von Chris Wright mit dem Angebot kontaktiert, entweder ihre Dieselreserven anzuzapfen, oder ein Exportverbot von US-Diesel zu riskieren.

item.title: [Financial Times] Accenture shares surge 22% as consultancy confounds AI fears
item.description: Group says revenues could accelerate in the coming year despite worries over demand for its services

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Le Pen and Mélenchon are ‘economically illiterate’ and weaponising migration, says French scholar ahead of 2027 race
item.description: French political scientist Jacques Rupnik says the economic illiteracy of Marine Le Pen and Mélenchon is astonishing. He anticipates that in the first round of France's presidential election, most voters will back a candidate they believe can stop Le Pen. A Mamdani moment could happen, since people feel that politics has exhausted itself.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: How does Trump’s AI pact compare with the EU?
item.description: Donald Trump is betting on voluntary commitments from AI companies. On Tuesday (29 September), he unveiled a self-regulatory agreement drawn up with some of the biggest names in the AI industry.

item.title: [Financial Times] An AI sovereign wealth fund isn’t progressive — it’s techno-imperialism
item.description: Accruing income at home from land and power abroad has an old name: empire

item.title: [EU Observer] EU accession of Moldova and Ukraine is alternative to Nato, as Russia draws new Iron Curtain in Europe
item.description: With Nato doors closed to Ukraine and Russia pushing a new Iron Curtain across the Black Sea, an “urgent” EU expansion toward Kyiv and Chișinău is emerging as Europe’s main tool to defend its eastern flank and preserve its global clout.

item.title: [Financial Times] Flydubai scare revives Israel’s hijacking trauma
item.description: Air travel for Israelis has been shaped by a long and painful history of assaults on planes

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s children will inherit public-health crisis from new EU pesticide approvals
item.description: By extending pesticide approvals and keeping hazardous products on the market, Brussels is bending to Big Pharma and causing a food-system and public-health burden for decades to come.

item.title: [Financial Times] Four potential positives from higher bond yields
item.description: The sharp rise in borrowing costs has raised justified alarm but there are benefits too

item.title: [EU Observer] Inside Poland’s fake student scheme: cheap labour, bogus visas and Russian ties
item.description: In Poland, student status has become a sought-after commodity that employment agencies exploit for gains. Many foreign workers were unaware they were enrolled in fake schools associated with pro-Kremlin figures.

item.title: [EU Observer] AI chatbots turn users’ most intimate data into a potential goldmine for advertisers, researchers warn
item.description: Researchers found that even when users rejected non-essential cookies, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Gemini, Copilot, ChatGPT and Claude still connected to Google Ads.

item.title: [Financial Times] An optimist’s guide to the bond market
item.description: It could be a lot worse. Really!

item.title: [Financial Times] Manchester City chair shielded by diplomatic immunity
item.description: Khaldoon al-Mubarak was granted immunity six years ago, protecting him from potential legal proceedings in the UK

item.title: [Financial Times] OpenAI’s agents obscured hacking activity in government site breaches
item.description: New findings by Asymmetric Security provide further evidence of novel tactics AI tools use to conduct hacks

item.title: [Financial Times] How Europe can stall Russia’s hybrid war
item.description: Enhancing domestic security, using new technologies and negotiating guardrails could lessen the risk of mass-casualty events

item.title: [Financial Times] Auditor RSM explores IPO to ward off private equity-backed rivals
item.description: Accounting firm has been sounding out bankers and revamping internal systems to give itself the option of a stock market flotation

item.title: [Financial Times] Tencent leases 100,000 chips from Oracle to accelerate AI push
item.description: WeChat owner strikes deal to access US group’s south-east Asia data centres amid race with ByteDance and Alibaba

item.title: [DW] European cities seek ways of boosting affordable housing
item.description: In many major urban centers of Europe, the housing shortage has become an explosive social issue. DW looks into various models that have been put in place across the continent.

item.title: [DW] Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
item.description: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.

item.title: [DW] Russia expected to intensify hybrid war on Europe
item.description: Drone explosions, airspace violations, arson attacks: Poland, Romania, and Moldova are now regularly targeted in Russian attacks against Ukraine. More governments are calling these attacks deliberate acts of aggression.

item.title: [DW] Russian classroom propaganda glorifies dying for your country, students say
item.description: The Russian government has stepped up its efforts to spread patriotic propaganda in schools. DW spoke to students about textbooks that portray the West as hostile and promote sacrifice for the nation.

item.title: [DW] Sicily: Mount Etna ash disrupts Catania flights again
item.description: A thick ash cloud from Mount Etna has been disrupting flights to Catania in Sicily for several days. Italy and Europe's most active volcano, Etna has impacted air travel several times this summer.

item.title: [DW] Turkey: Comedian convicted for 'insulting' Erdogan in show
item.description: Deniz Goktas was convicted of two of three charges, including "insulting" the president, but was released pending the appeal process. Nominally, Turkey is a secular country with free speech.

item.title: [DW] What would Francis of Assisi make of his fame today?
item.description: The Catholic saint renounced wealth and fame to become a mendicant friar. Yet throughout history, his teachings and life have inspired popes, Dante and even Mussolini.
